component.name: Depot
component.summary: See, update and remove every app on your computer

description.p: Linux software comes from many places: your distribution's own packages, Snap, Flatpak, downloaded archives and more. Depot puts all of it in one window, tells you in plain language how each app was installed, and updates or removes it the right way, so you don't need to know which command to use.
Depot is made for people who are new to Linux:

ul.li: Every app in one place, with a badge saying whether it's a Deb, RPM, Pacman, Snap, Flatpak or manual install
One card per app, even when it's installed more than one way
Tick several apps and uninstall them together, or tick exactly which updates to install
Before anything is removed, Depot shows exactly what will go with it
Apps installed by hand go to the Trash, so you can change your mind
Finds broken launchers left behind in your app menu
Select several apps and uninstall them together
Tick exactly which updates to install
A progress window that says when your password was accepted and how everything went
Safer clean-up of apps installed by hand
An About window with the licence, privacy and legal notices

description.p: Updates page, removal through PackageKit, and support for RPM and Pacman systems.
